boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all three frozen records in Iuka and Corinth Operations. Preserve per-engagement dates: Iuka September 19, Corinth October 3–4 and Hatchie's Bridge October 5. The live NPS campaign heading does not replace any battle interval. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force fields give approx. 4,000–4,500 US (2nd and cavalry divisions) and approx. 3,200 CS (1st Division); the live field reads zero. NPS says Price had about 14,000 men. Greene gives Rosecrans's column about 9,000 and Ord's about 6,000, says Hamilton brought 2,800 into action, and that two Confederate brigades of three to four thousand did the fighting.
claims.rationale: Army, column, engaged-division and brigade figures are different populations; none is adopted as a matched opening strength. Ord's column did not engage.

claims.value: NPS says Rosecrans stated he left the Fulton road unguarded for fear of dividing his force, and that Grant approved; Greene says Rosecrans, forced into action on arriving, had no opportunity to move onto that road. Grant had ordered Ord to wait for the sound of fighting.
claims.rationale: The sources give different reasons for the open road; neither is adopted. The listed commanders do not receive automatic sole credit for the combined operation.

claims.value: The frozen result is Union victory, with a note that it caused Grant concern about Rosecrans's abilities; the live field reads Union Victory. Both sources say Price escaped by the Fulton road.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The frozen note is a source annotation, not a measured effect.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,482 total (US 782; CS 700); the live NPS field reads 1384 total (US 790; CS 594;). Greene gives Rosecrans's reported 782 and Price's reported 496, against a provost-marshal tally of 1,438 including prisoners and an estimate of wounded carried off.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The provost-marshal total includes an estimate and prisoners; it is not adopted.

open_questions: Returns, Confederate casualty reconciliation and the Grant–Rosecrans–Ord message chronology remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family; Greene is one retrospective history by a non-participant Union engineer officer, founded on the Official Records. Reports quoted inside Greene are not additional independently inspected families.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
